functional_semantics.triton: out = x_f32 * tl.sigmoid(x_f32) * y_f32 cast to x.dtype over the flattened tensors (impl_triton.py 18-23, 41-44, 57).
functional_semantics.cutile: out = x_tile * (1/(1+ct.exp(-x_tile))) * y_tile in fp32 cast to x.dtype over the flattened tensors (impl_cutile.py 24-28, 37-40, 64).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise F.silu(x) * y (impl_torch.py 5); the sigmoid builtin versus the explicit exp formula is a primitive choice within tolerance.

stages.triton: One kernel, one launch, grid = ceil(M*N/block) (47, 51).

precision.triton: Both operands .to(tl.float32) (20-21), fp32 sigmoid and products (22), explicit .to(x.dtype) at the store (23).
precision.cutile: Both operands ct.astype(ct.float32) (24-25), fp32 exp/add/divide/products (26-27), one ct.astype to x.dtype (27).
precision.note: fp32 evaluation with a single downcast on both sides.

preprocessing.triton: assert shapes equal; x.contiguous().view(-1), y.contiguous().view(-1), torch.empty_like(x_flat), output.view(x.shape) (40-44, 57).
preprocessing.cutile: assert shapes equal; same flattening views, torch.empty_like(x_flat), output.view(x.shape) (36-40, 64).
preprocessing.note: Views plus one output allocation inside run() on both sides; no copy, cast or cached state.

mutation.triton: x, y read-only; fresh output each call (43).
mutation.cutile: x, y read-only; fresh output each call (39); tuning launches overwrite output (49), rewritten by the final launch.
mutation.note: No input mutation; idempotent; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: n is engine-provided: infer_problem_size('swiglu') has no explicit branch and falls back to the product of all integer case params = M*N (tilebench/data/tensors.py 778-784, used via core/metrics.py 61), i.e. the element count. Both timed run() bodies perform only flattening views and one empty allocation besides the kernel, which reads x and y once and writes the output once, exactly what bytes_expr counts (config.yaml 18). flops_expr is the nominal one-operation-per-element convention.
